## Information about this section

This .qmd file was used to build the best boundary for the ridge regression using Youden's J-Statistic

I tried to do the same for Lasso Regression, but I didn't have time to get it working.

## Ridge Regression Boundary

```{r}
#We will be using the glmnet package for this section, following instructions from the ISLP textbook.
#We will begin with ridge regression

#Set up X and Y
x <- model.matrix(surgery ~ release_speed + arm_angle + spin_axis + release_spin_rate + pitch_type + release_pos_z  
                  , data = data_complete_na)[,-1]
y <- data_complete_na$surgery
#Set up grid and fitting the ridge regression model
grid <- 10^seq(10, -2, length = 100)
ridge.mod <- glmnet(x,y, alpha = 0, lambda = grid)

#Size of our matrix
#dim(coef(ridge.mod))
```

```{r}
#Create our training/testing data
train <- sample(1:nrow(x), nrow(x) * 0.8)  
test <- (-train)
y.test <- y[test]
```

```{r}
#Get the prediction class for our model and set as a factor.
ridge.pred.prob <- predict(ridge.mod, s = 4, newx = x[test,], type = "response")

# Convert probabilities to class predictions
# Make sure you know what your surgery levels are
data_complete_na$surgery <- as.factor(data_complete_na$surgery)

ridge_pred_class <- ifelse(ridge.pred.prob > 0.285, 
                          levels(data_complete_na$surgery)[2], 
                          levels(data_complete_na$surgery)[1])
ridge_pred_class <- as.factor(ridge_pred_class)

# Get actual test values
actual_class <- data_complete_na$surgery[test]

# Create confusion matrix
ridge_conf <- confusionMatrix(ridge_pred_class, 
                             actual_class,
                             positive = levels(actual_class)[2])

print(ridge_conf)
```

```{r}
library(pROC)

# Step 1 — Get predicted probabilities (same as before)
ridge.pred.prob <- predict(ridge.mod, s = 4, newx = x[test,], type = "response")

# Step 2 — Find optimal threshold using Youden's J
actual_class <- data_complete_na$surgery[test]

roc_obj <- roc(actual_class, as.vector(ridge.pred.prob))

best_youden <- coords(roc_obj, x="best", input="threshold", best.method="youden")
print(best_youden)

optimal_threshold <- best_youden$threshold

# Step 3 — Apply optimal threshold instead of hardcoded 0.285
data_complete_na$surgery <- as.factor(data_complete_na$surgery)

ridge_pred_class <- ifelse(ridge.pred.prob > optimal_threshold,
                           levels(data_complete_na$surgery)[2],
                           levels(data_complete_na$surgery)[1])
ridge_pred_class <- as.factor(ridge_pred_class)

# Step 4 — Confusion matrix
ridge_conf <- confusionMatrix(ridge_pred_class,
                              actual_class,
                              positive = levels(actual_class)[2])
print(ridge_conf)

# Step 5 — Optional: plot ROC curve with the chosen threshold marked
plot(roc_obj, print.auc = TRUE, print.thres = "best",
     main = "Ridge Regression ROC Curve")
```

```{r}
#Create our training/testing data
train <- sample(1:nrow(x), nrow(x) * 0.8)  
test <- (-train)
y.test <- y[test]

ridge.mod <- glmnet(x[train,], y[train], alpha = 0, lambda = grid, thresh = 1e-12)
ridge.pred <- predict(ridge.mod, s = 4, newx = x[test,])
#Test MSE
mean((ridge.pred - y.test)^2)

#Find the best lambda
cv.out <- cv.glmnet(x[train,], y[train], alpha = 0)
plot(cv.out)

#Best lambda actual calculation
bestlam <- cv.out$lambda.min
bestlam

#Coefficients
out <- glmnet(x, y, alpha = 0)
predict(out, type = "coefficients", s = bestlam)[1:13,]
```

## Lasso Regression

```{r}
lasso.mod <- glmnet(x[train,], y[train],alpha = 1, lambda = grid, importance = TRUE)
plot(lasso.mod, label = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#Get the prediction class for our model and set as a factor.
lasso.pred.prob <- predict(lasso.mod, s = 4, newx = x[test,], type = "response")
data_complete_na$surgery <- as.factor(data_complete_na$surgery)

# Convert probabilities to class predictions
actual_class <- data_complete_na$surgery[test]

roc_obj <- roc(actual_class, as.vector(lasso.pred.prob))

best_youden <- coords(roc_obj, x="best", input="threshold", best.method="youden")
print(best_youden)

optimal_threshold <- best_youden$threshold

lasso_pred_class <- ifelse(lasso.pred.prob > optimal_threshold, 
                          levels(data_complete_na$surgery)[2], 
                          levels(data_complete_na$surgery)[1])
lasso_pred_class <- as.factor(lasso_pred_class)

# Get actual test values
actual_class <- data_complete_na$surgery[test]

# Create confusion matrix
lasso_conf <- confusionMatrix(lasso_pred_class, 
                             actual_class,
                             positive = levels(actual_class)[2])

print(lasso_conf)

plot(roc_obj, print.auc = TRUE, print.thres = "best",
     main = "Ridge Regression ROC Curve")
```
